briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF M-010
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- water tower top: (81, -60), roof
- north roof: (-7, 53), roof
- workshop: (90, 95), indoor
- control room: (62, 140), indoor
- east fence: (-86, -2), outdoor
- fuel depot: (-102, 134), outdoor
- gate 2: (49, -119), outdoor

Robots:
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 8 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 960 s, including the return to its start.
- G1 (rover): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 2.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 25 kg), camera. Endurance: 5280 s, including the return to its start.
- D2 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 6 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 1440 s, including the return to its start.
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 6 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3060 s, including the return to its start.
- M2 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 7 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 2520 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Run a thermal scan of east fence. Location: east fence. Duration: 90 s. Needs: thermal camera. Deadline: finished by t = 180 s.
- T2: Deliver the cable reel (14 kg) to control room. Location: control room. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 14 kg).
- T3: Deliver the toolkit (14 kg) to east fence. Location: east fence. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 14 kg).
- T4: Replace the filter cartridge at control room. Location: control room. Duration: 240 s. Needs: robotic arm. Deadline: finished by t = 960 s. Can start only after T2 is finished.
- T5: Deliver the first-aid kit (7 kg) to gate 2. Location: gate 2. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 7 kg).
- T6: Deliver the pressure gauge (2 kg) to east fence. Location: east fence. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 2 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 120 s.
- T7: Deliver the cable reel (12 kg) to gate 2. Location: gate 2. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 12 kg).
- T8: Deliver the replacement filter (3 kg) to east fence. Location: east fence. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 3 kg).
- T9: Tighten the valve at gate 2. Location: gate 2. Duration: 270 s. Needs: robotic arm. Deadline: finished by t = 780 s. Can start only after T7 is finished.
- T10: Tighten the valve at east fence. Location: east fence. Duration: 300 s. Needs: robotic arm. Can start only after T3 is finished.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 1200 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Hi team, here is today's job at the site.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: water tower top (81, -60, a rooftop); north roof (-7, 53, a rooftop); workshop (90, 95, indoors); control room (62, 140, indoors); east fence (-86, -2, outside); fuel depot (-102, 134, outside); gate 2 (49, -119, outside).

The fleet: D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera; it flies at 8 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 16 minutes including the flight home. G1 is a rover parked at base that hauls up to 25 kg at 2.5 m/s and runs for 88 minutes including the drive back. It has a camera. D2, a quadcopter waiting at base, carries a camera and a thermal camera, cruises at 6 m/s, lifts up to 2 kg and has 24 minutes of flight time, return trip included. M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 6 kg, moves at 1 m/s and lasts 51 minutes including getting back. M2 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 7 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 42 minutes including getting back.

Jobs:
(T1) Look for overheating equipment around east fence - that takes 1.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 3 minutes.
(T2) Drop the cable reel off at control room; it weighs 14 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T3) East fence needs the toolkit, which weighs 14 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.
(T4) Change the filter at control room - that takes 4 minutes on site but only once the cable reel (T2) has arrived and it has to be finished within the first 16 minutes.
(T5) Get the first-aid kit (7 kg) over to gate 2 - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.
(T6) East fence needs the pressure gauge, which weighs 2 kg - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 2 minutes.
(T7) Gate 2 needs the cable reel, which weighs 12 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T8) Drop the replacement filter off at east fence; it weighs 3 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T9) The valve at gate 2 needs tightening - that takes 4.5 minutes on site but only once the cable reel (T7) has arrived and it has to be finished within the first 13 minutes.
(T10) The valve at east fence needs tightening - that takes 5 minutes on site but only once the toolkit (T3) has arrived.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 20 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
